Lab 076 · Lesson 076 · simulation using the lesson's numbers

Open World Lab

The Reef's archipelago has 12 islands, and the first build loads all of them and simulates every fish, boat and villager. On the dev kit it runs at 44 ms and uses 11.0 GB; the handheld has 3.5 GB for the game. Choose what is loaded, how it streams, how distant islands are drawn and how far the world is simulated in full.

A free camera over 12 islands, on the handheld. Goal: 3.5 GB or less, 30 fps (33.3 ms or less), no frame over 50 ms while you sail, loading in 20 s or less, and every island still on the horizon.

Lesson 076: optimizing an open world

    What this shows

    Memory is about what's loaded

    Smaller textures shrink every island; streaming decides how many islands exist in memory at all. An open world needs the second first.

    Streaming must not block

    Loading near the player is right; doing it on the game thread turns every cell boundary into a hitch. Load in the background, activate a little each frame.

    Far away needs a cheap stand-in

    Unloaded islands still belong on the horizon. One HLOD mesh per island keeps them there for a few draws, and the simulation far away can be coarse too.

    This lab is a model, not a measurement. It uses Lesson 076's numbers for the archipelago on the handheld. Memory: 1.4 GB for engine, code, audio and UI, plus 0.3 GB of geometry and 0.5 GB of textures per loaded island (0.2 GB with mip streaming), plus 0.2 GB for all HLOD proxies. Streaming keeps the 3 islands within 1 km loaded. Game thread: 44 ms simulating all 6,000 agents in full, 18 ms with full simulation within 300 m and coarse simulation beyond. Render thread and GPU: 41 and 38 ms with every island in full detail, 16 and 26 ms with HLOD proxies, 12 and 22 ms if distant islands aren't drawn at all. The frame is the slowest stage (Lesson 075). A blocking cell load costs a 240 ms frame; async loading adds about 4 ms to a frame. Loading: 95 s for everything, 70 s with mip streaming, 12 s when streaming.
